content: ʿAbd al-Razzāq Kirmānī (fl. 900/1495), writing his Niʿmatullahi hagiography at the request of Niʿmat Allāh II, reports that Ṣāʾin al-Dīn and Sharaf al-Dīn Yazdī sought audience with Niʿmat Allāh at Kūnubān (Kūhbanān, near Kirman); he adds that he heard they went to Syria to become disciples of Sayyid Ḥusayn Akhlāṭī at Niʿmat Allāh's direction and learned the letters of jafr 'from that eminence' (MK's translation leaves the antecedent unclear). MK: the author's concern is to stress the deference of the two men to Niʿmat Allāh and to credit Niʿmat Allāh with initiating the discipleship under Akhlāṭī.
refers_to_primary: ʿAbd al-Razzāq Kirmānī, Tazkira dar Manāqib-i Ḥażrat Shāh Niʿmat Allāh Valī (Aubin, Majmūʿa, 70)
